NJ Jose Marti STEM Academy.lab_feedback: This year, our Hydroponic Classroom evolved into much more than a traditional growing space. It became a multidisciplinary STEM hub that connected biology, sustainability, nutrition, wellness, entrepreneurship, and community engagement. Students participated not only in growing food, but also in designing outreach initiatives, producing value-added products, exploring food access/community wellness concepts, and leading public-facing educational activities.  One of the biggest successes was seeing students take ownership of authentic projects with visible real-world impact. The systems and curriculum provided by NY Sun Works created an excellent foundation for this type of hands-on learning.  Areas that would help us improve even further next year include additional operational/planning support for teachers managing large-scale hydroponic spaces, easier access to replacement supplies/materials, and expanded advanced resources for schools interested in scaling beyond introductory hydroponics into broader sustainability, food systems, and research-based programming.  Overall, the Hydroponic Classroom continues to be one of the most engaging and impactful educational environments in our school.
NJ Jose Marti STEM Academy.curr_feedback: The NY Sun Works curriculum and infrastructure provided an excellent foundation for hands-on STEM learning and helped us expand hydroponics into a broader interdisciplinary program. Over time, our classroom evolved beyond traditional hydroponic instruction into a student-centered ecosystem involving sustainability, nutrition, food systems, wellness, entrepreneurship, and community engagement.    One area that could be especially valuable moving forward would be more advanced/scalable professional development and curriculum pathways for schools that are ready to move beyond introductory hydroponics. Examples could include food systems science, community impact projects, hydroponic entrepreneurship, sustainability leadership, culinary integration, data collection/analytics, student research projects, and cross-curricular implementation at the high school level.    Additional operational support resources for teachers managing large student-led hydroponic programs would also be extremely helpful, especially around long-term system maintenance, crop planning, advanced growing strategies, and scaling harvest/community distribution efforts.    Overall, the Hydroponic Classroom remains one of the most engaging and impactful learning spaces in our school, and students consistently demonstrate increased ownership, collaboration, and real-world problem solving through the program.
